content:
- Overestimate prices after recent spikes (especially when sentiment is positive or neutral); model tends to overshoot early in the 30-day horizon.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., sentiment < -0.5) — model is overly cautious, missing upward momentum.
- Lag in price correction: model often delays downward adjustments after negative sentiment spikes, especially in the first 5–7 days.
- Mean reversion bias: model overcorrects after sharp rallies (e.g., +10%+ in 3–5 days) and fails to account for lingering volatility.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts are overly optimistic in the first 10–15 days when sentiment is volatile; later days (16–30) show better alignment but still lag behind true trend.
- Sentiment-driven bias: when sentiment is > 1.0, model tends to overreact to bullish signals; when sentiment < -0.5, model underreacts to bearish signals.
